FORTHCOMING AGRICULTITRA.L SHOW AT LIVERPOOL: SHOW OF CATTLE ARANDoNED.—A general meeting of the members of the Royal Manchester, Liverpool, and North Lancashire Agricultural Society was held on Wednesday at the showyard, Newsham Park, Liverpool, Lord Winmar- leigh presiding. Having regard to the exi,tence of foot- and-mouth disease within the district where the show is to be held, the meeting decided not to hold the show of cattle, sheep, and pigs, confining the exhibition to horses, dogs, poultry, implements, dm. Lord Winmarleigh. in proposing success to the forthcoming show at the luncheon following the meeting, said that he thought the Agricultural Holdings Act would be found, as a whole, most catisfactory both to landlords and tenants. He believed, too, that the landlords of the country would meet their tenants under the new Act with the same feeling as formerly. For himself he could only say that he should honestly and zealously carry out the provisions of the new enactment, and he hoped that under it both landlords and tenants might meet with great prosperity.

The Lymm Volunteer Company had an interesting Out_ pst and tactical drill in Agden Park, by permission of Mr. Birch, on Saturday last. The idea to be worked out was that a strong infantry patrol had been dispatched from a force assembled near Bowdon with orders to endeavour to penetrate the out-post line of a force encamped in the neigh- bourhood of Lymm, and get the best possible idea of the position and strength of the same. At four in the afternoon the company paraded at the village cross, and marched to Agden under the direction of Captain Bower and Lieutenant Blair, the efficient little bugle band which has lately become part of the corps playing lively marches during the greater part of the route. After a short halt, outside ' Agden Park, Lieutenant Blair proceeded along the main road with the right half company to represent the before-mentioned patrol from Bowdon. while Captain Bower entered the park with the left half company and stationed it as an out-post picket, with double sentries so placed as to command views of the ground and all the approaches north-east of Agilen Hall. After the lapse of about an hour, which was etnployPd by Captain Bower's party in the usual outpost work of Patrolling, signalling, atc., Lieutenant Blair's scouts were described approaching from the direction of Newfield covert. These were allowed to come within abeut, 300 yards of the line of the sentries—of whose proximity they evidently had no suspicion—when a rather amusing incident occurred in the capture of one of the scouts, who at first offered a stout resistance, but was obliged in the end to submit to the superiority of numbers. Presently the whole of Lieutenant Blair's party was seen to cross Agden Brook and move up the slope with the probable intention of making straight for the crest line occupied by the picket sentries. Meanwhile Captain Bower—having decided to make his stand on this line, which afforded tolerable cover and gave the best possible zone of fire—had brought up the rest of his picket and placed his men under cover with a full sweep of the ground to the front. It was, therefore, with but little chance of effecting his purpose, though with considerable energy and judgment, that Lieutenant Blair rushed up the hill by alternate sections under what certainly would have been a withering fire. As the assailants neared the posi- tion, flank counter-attacks were made by detached portions of the defenders' line, and the last of these, though smartly met by a partial change of front, brought the drill to an end, with the result that the attack on the outpost line had completely failed.

PIGEON SHOOTING MATCH FOR £lOO.—A match, which created no small amount of interest, was decided in the most satisfactory manner on Monday last, at Abbey Hey Park, Gorton, near Manchester. The opponents—two cele- brities—were J. Welsby. of Warrington, and It. Bates, at Ince, near Wigan, and the conditions were to shoot at 25 pigeons each, loz. shot, H and T traps, 21 yards rise and 60 fall, for £5O a-side. Both men are well-known, have berg enjoyed a first-class reputation, and are supposed to have very few, if any, superiors in England. All the greater in- terest, therefore, was centred in the contest, as they had never before opposed each other in a match. There was a pretty numerous attendance of spectators, who numbered about 400. A great many perscns were present from War- rington, and they heartily cheered their representative whenever he succeeded in bringing down his bird; whilst Bates' followers pinned their faith on his invincibility.i Bates, however, was beaten, but only by a single bird, after one of the best contested and most pleasant matches that have been decided at the above grounds or anywhere else. The shooting on the part of both men was of such a first- class character as to call forth the warmest enconniums of all present. Before starting odds of sto 4 were laid 1 lon Bates. The favourite k;lled his first pair of birds in sue- cession in capital style, whilst Welsby missed his third, and Bates allowed his fifth to escape. The pair were on level terms at the esventh round, and so continued until almost the very close. Each f .iled to bring down his eighth bird, when Welsby grassed 14 in succession. Bates, wbo was shooting in good form, brought down 12 in succession, when he missed two, and Welshy for the first time took the lead. Unfortunitely his 23rd bird escap,cl and redueed his lead, and raised the hopes of Bates' party ; but Welsby killed his last two, and thus won a closely-contested and exciting match all through. Out of the seven birds missed only three got clear away, the others having fallen a few yards outside the boundary. Mr. T. It. Allison, of Manchester, officiated as refgee.

BOWLING MATCH: GREEN AND BALL FOR £5O.—.J. Green, of Blatkburn, and G. Ball, of Warrington, met on the Whitebirk Green, Blackburn, on Thursday afternoon, to play the first of two home and home games of 101 up, for a stake of £5O. The weather was nice and fine and a large number of spectators were present. The bowlers were not allowed to change their woods, and betting on the match was 6to 4 on Green, and 3 to 1 on him for the first game. The most interesting item in the betting, however, was in Green's friends laying even money that their man won by 30 points. This he seemed more than likely of accomplish- ing at one time, but the finish saw him only 27 points to the good. After standing at sto 4, Green ran to 13 to 5, 16 to 12, and 27 to 12; but Ball then got to 17 against 30, and at the interval the scores stood—Green 51, Ball 37. On resuming, Green got to 64 against 43, G 9 to 50, 78 to 55, and 84 to 62, when the Blackburn man ran to 89. Here Ball replied with seven; Green, however, kept the lead to the finish, and won easily. Score: Green, 101; Ball, 74 —The return match w;lt b! played on the King and Queen Green Padgate, near Warrington, on Monday.

Brailey, M.D. Dental Burgeon—H. Mon, Esq. Aural Surgeon—W. Laidlaw Purves, Esq. Medical Registrar—R E. Carrington, M.D. Surgical Registrar—J. Poland, Esq. Instructor in Anasthetics—T. Bird, Esq. The Hospital contains, besides the beds for Medical and Sur- gical cases, wards for Obstetric, Ophthalmic, and other special departments. In connection with the Lying-in-Charity, about 2,500 cases are annually attended by the Students. Number of patients relieved during the year. about 80,000. LECTURES, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND PRACTICAL •COURSES. Medicine—Dr. Pavy and Dr. Moxon. Clinical Medicine—Dr. Wilks, Dr. Pavy, Dr. Moxon, and Dr. Fagge. Surgery—Mr. Bryant and Mr. Durham. Clinical Surgery—Mr. Bryant, Mr. Durham, Mr. Howse, and ker. Davies-Colley. Practical Surgery—Mr. Clement Lucas. Clinical Lectures on Midwifery and Diseases of Women—Dr. Galabin. "Morbid Anatomy—Dr. Goodhart and Dr. Mahomed. Cutaneous Diseases—Dr. Pye-limitb. Anatomy (De_criptive and Surgical) Mr. Howse and Mr. Daviez-Colley. Practical Anatomy—Dr. White, Mr. Lane, Mr. Price, and Two Assistant Demonstrators. Physiology—Dr. Pye-Smith. Practical Physiology—Mr. Golding-Bird. Chemistry—Dr. Steveuson and Mr. Groves. Experimental Physics—Prof. A. W. Remote, F.R.S. Practical Pharmacy—lnstruction is given in the Hospital Dis- pensary. Clinical Lectures in Medicine, Surgery, and Midwifery weekly. Special Class,s are held in the Hospital for Students pre- paring for the Examinations of the University of London and of the College of Surgeons. The Museum of Anatomy, Pathology, and Comparative Ana- tomy—Curator, Dr. Goudhart— contains 11,000 specimens, 4,500 drawings and diagrams, a unique collection of Anatomical Models, and a series of 600 Models of Skin Diseases. APPornTmErrs.—The House Surgeons and House Physicians, the Obstetric Residents, Clinical Assistants; and Dressers are selected from the Students according to merit and without pay- mrnt. There are also a large number of Junior appointments, every part of the Hospital Practice being 53 stematically em- ployed for instruction. ' EarrlLuscE ECHOLARSHIPS. Open Scholarship of 125 guineas. in Classics, Mathematics. and Modern Languages. Open r cholarship of 125 guineas, in Chemistry, Physics, Botany and Zoo'ogy.
